instruction: Using LibreOffice Writer, combine every .txt file in your VSCode project folder into 'merged_doc.docx' on the Desktop, ensuring the whole document uses font size 12 and no separators are added.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5)

metadata.explanation: Task requires merging all 5 txt files (1.txt through 5.txt) in order and setting font size to 12. Evaluator checks if the merged content matches the expected concatenated text from all files and font size is 12pt. Added postconfig to save the document with Ctrl+S before evaluation to ensure LibreOffice Writer persists the changes.
metadata.verification: Verified by reading all 5 txt files from cache. Total concatenated length: 2249 characters. Expected font size: 12pt.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: 0.5 for correct merged content, 0.5 for correct font size (12pt)

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts content with no separators using ''.join(content) (getters/docx.py:42), matching instruction 'Do not add any separators'
Getter verifies ALL runs in ALL paragraphs for font_size=12pt (getters/docx.py:44-74), correctly implementing 'entire document' requirement
Metric uses exact string comparison (metrics/docx.py:32) without normalization, correctly matching expected_content format
Postconfig includes Ctrl+S to save document before evaluation, ensuring state is persisted

Minor issue: Getter treats runs with no explicit font.size as non-12pt (getters/docx.py:60-61), which could cause false negatives if runs inherit 12pt from document style. However, this is conservative and likely acceptable for validation.

Minor issue: Content is stripped (.strip() on lines 66, 72) which could cause mismatch if expected_content has intentional leading/trailing whitespace, though this is unlikely for concatenated txt files.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider handling inherited font sizes: Check if run.font.size is None but paragraph/document style is 12pt, or ensure all text has explicit font size set during document creation
Verify expected_content matches the exact output format (with or without leading/trailing whitespace) to ensure .strip() operation doesn't cause mismatches
